newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Woodside shares capture new highs.
newsitem.headline: Woodside shares capture new highs.

text.p: Shares in oil and gas major Woodside Petroleum Ltd moved to a record high of A$10.05 on Tuesday after Monday's formal approval of development funding for the Laminaria/Corallina oil project in the Timor Sea.

The oil fields are estimated to have combined recoverable oil reserves of between 130 and 150 million barrels with the development to boast the world's largest floating production and storage (FPSO) facility.
The platform is to be located in about 360 metres of water about 550 kilometres west northwest of Darwin.
Woodside holds 50 percent of the venture while Shell and BHP each hold 25 percent.

"They have had some good news lately," said a dealer at a Melbourne-based brokerage, pointing to the Laminaria approval and the announcement on April 16 of sales to the U.S. of liquified natural gas (LNG) from the North West Shelf project.
By 11.40 a.m. (0140 GMT), Woodside shares had ventured further into record territory to be 18 cents higher at A$10.07 on turnover of 986,129 shares.
